violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: RAW BEEF PATTIES WERE BEING STORED NEXT TO READY TO EAT VEGETABLES IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL RAW FOODS MUST ALWAYS BE STORED BELOW READY TO EAT FOODS TO PREVENT THE POTENTIAL SPREAD OF BACTERIA. PIC MOVED THE RAW BUGER PATTIES TO BELOW THE READY TO EAT VEGETABLES IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. COOKED BARBACOA IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR WAS TEMPING AT 51 DEGREES, TWO DAYS AFTER BEING COOKED.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL COOKED FOODS MUST COOL WITHIN 6 HOURS TO PREVENT THE GROWTH OF BACTERIA. SINCE THE COOKED BARBACOA IS TEMPING AT 51 DEGREES LONGER THAN 6 HOURS AFTER BEING COOKED, PIC THREW AWAY THE BARBACOA AT TIME OF INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: BARBACOA WAS BEING STORED IN TALL METAL CONTAINER WITH A LID THAT DID NOT ALLOW FOR AIR FOOW AND PROPER COOLING OF THE BARBACOA AFTER BEING COOKED.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC PROPER WAYS TO FACILITATE COOLING. DUE TO THE TEMPERATURE OF THE BARBACOA BEING HIGH AND NOT COOLING PROPERLY, PIC THREW WAY BARBACOA AT TIME OF INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. JUGS OF LIQUID BUTTER WERE BEING STORED ON THE FLOOR IN THE KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOODS MUST BE STORED AT LEAST 6 INCHES OFF OF THE GROUND. PIC MOVED THE LIQUID BUTTER TO A SHELVING UNIT NEAR BY SO THEY WERE NO LONGER BEING STORED ON THE GROUND.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT SANITIZER TOWLES MUST BE STORED IN SANITIZER SOLUTION IN BETWEN USES. PLEASE MAKE SURE ALL SANITIZER TOWLES ARE PROPERLY STORED AT TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours

violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. PLEASE ENSURE FOODS ARE COOLED FROM 135F TO 70F IN 2 HOURS AND TO A FURTHER 41F WITHIN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS USING PROPER COOLING METHODS.

violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: BEEF BARBACOA AT 54F AND BEANS AT 44F IN DEEP COVERED PANS PREPARED THE PREVIOUS DAY IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: FROZEN BEEF TONGUE THAWING IN STANDING WATER IN BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO TRANSFER BEEF TONGUE TO WALK IN REFRIGERATOR TO CONTINUE THAWING.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Charro beans in the walk-in refrigerator were temping at a range of 48F-52F over 24 hours after being prepared.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: 2DWR under grill cooler on the left is not working properly and was temping at 110F at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PIC WAS AWARE OF THE BROKEN PIECE OF EQUIPMENT AND HAD ALREADY CALLED A REPAIR COMPANY PRIOR TO THE DAY OF INSPECTION. THE REPAIR COMPANY WAS COMING THE SAME DAY AS THE INSPECTION TO LOOK AT/FIX UNIT. PIC WILL EMAIL EHS A PICTURE OF THE UNIT WITH A CLEAR PIC OF THE TEMPERATURE GAUGE ON THE FRONT OF UNIT SHOWING 41F OR BELOW, ONCE FIXED.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: Employee who was cooking an allergen, did not wash their hands or change gloves before cooking chicken along side the allergen. Employee just placed new gloves over his dirty gloves.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS EXPLAINED TO PIC AND EMPLOYEES WHEN THEY NEED TO WASH HANDS AND CHANGE GLOVES IN BETWEEN TASKS. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE WASH HANDS AND PUT ON NEW GLOVES.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. PIC WILL GET HAND WASHING SIGNS FOR EACH HAND SINK BY TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: different types of frozen meat in the walk- in refrigerator where being stored incorrectly and not in order of cook temps.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). EHS EXPLAINED TO PIC THAT ALL RAW FOOD, EVEN FROZEN, NEEDS TO BE ORGANIZED IN THE ORDER OF COOK TEMPS FROM LOWEST TO HIGHEST COOK TEMP. PIC REARRANGED THE FROZEN MEAT IN THE WALK-IN FREEZER TO BE IN THE CORRECT ORDER.

violations.title: Food Contact Surface, Clean between Raw Animal Foods
violations.observation: Equipment food contact surfaces/utensils were not observed cleaned before each use with a different type of raw animal food.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned before each use with a different type of raw animal food such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, or poultry. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT UTENSILS USED TO COOK AN ALLERGEN MUST BE CLEANED AND SANITIZED AFTER USE. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE SWITCH UTENSILS TO COOK SHRIMP AND TO COOK CHICKEN.

violations.title: Cooking Raw Animal Foods, Minimum of 165F
violations.observation: The following poultry item was not cooked to a sufficient temperature and/or time to eliminate pathogenic bacteria: Chicken was cooked to 156F and not the proper cook temp of 165F.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods such as poultry, wild game animals, stuffed fish, stuffed meat, stuffed pasta, stuffed poultry, stuffed ratites, or stuffing containing any of these raw animal foods shall be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 165F for at least 15 seconds. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT ALL POULTRY ITEMS NEEDS TO BE COOKED FULLY TO THE TEMP OF 165F. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE PUT THE CHICKEN BACK ON THE GRILL UNTIL IT REACHED A COOK TEMP OF 165F. THE FINAL COOK TEMP WAS 175F.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Chorizo (77f) and chicken (60f) were being stored improperly, and were not holding a temp a 135F or higher.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT ALL HOT FOODS NEED TO BE KEPT AT 135F OR HIGHER. THE CHORIZO AND CHICKEN WERE STILL IN THE 4 HOUR TIME BLOCK WHERE FOOD CAN BE REHEATED 165F TO KILL BACTERIA AND BE PROPERLY HOT HELD AFTERWARDS IN ORDER TO SERVE THE FOOD. BOTH THE CHORIZO AND CHICKEN WERE REHEATED TO 165F OR HIGHER.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: shredded cabbage was being stored improperly in an ice bath on a prep top unit. The cabbage was not fully submerged in the ice bath and was temping at 60F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT ALL COLD FOODS NEED TO COLD HELD AT 41F OR BELOW. PIC THREW AWAY CABBAGE THAT WAS TEMPING IMPROPERLY.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: multiple packages of ground beef were being stored under 3 vat sink at ambient temperature to thaw. Lingua and multiple containers of soup were being stored on a prep table at ambient temperature to thaw.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT FOOD CAN ONLY BE THAWED TWO WAYS; FROZEN FOOD IS MOVED FROM THE FREEZER TO A REFRIGERATOR UNTIL IT REACHES 41F OR FOOD CAN BE SUBMERGED UNDER WATER AND HAVE RUNNING WATER AT 70F CONTINUOUSLY RUNNING OVER THE FOOD UNTIL IT REACHES 41F. PIC HAD AN EMPLOYEE PUT ALL FOOD IMPROPERLY THAWING TO THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: multiple spray bottles around the kitchen and dish area were not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT ALL ITEMS TAKEN OUT OF ITS ORIGINAL CONTAINER NEEDS TO BE PROPERLY LABELED. PIC WILL LABEL SPRAY BOTTLES BY TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Dead or Trapped Pest Removed
violations.observation: Dead or trapped small insects were found in the light shield over the light in the dish pit.
violations.corrective_action: Remove dead rodents, birds, and insects from the premises to ensure that the establishment is clean and sanitary and to prevent carcasses from attracting other pests. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT THE DEAD BUGS IN THE LIGHT SHIELD NEED TO BE REMOVED AND CLEANED. PIC WILL TAKE CARE OF IT BY THE TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.corrective_action: Food may not be stored under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips. violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: plastic bags were being used as a cover over tortillas in oil. Plastic bags were also being used to store corn tortillas on a plate.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT PLASTIC BAGS ARE NOT ALLOWED TO BE USED IN THE FACILITY FOR FOOD STORAGE. PIC REMOVED THE PLASTIC BAGS BEING USED FOR FOOD STORAGE AND REPLACED IT WITH ALUMINUM FOIL.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): storage of multiple food items all around facility.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT SODA CRATES CANNOT BE USED FOR FOOD STORAGE BECAUSE THEY ARE DIFFICULT TO FULLY CLEAN AND SANITIZE. PIC WILL SWITCH SODA CRATES TO EASILY CLEANABLE CONTAINERS BY NEXT INSPECTION.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not resistant to corrosion: facility was using construction equipment (Dewalt and Husky scrapers) to clean the grill in between uses.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT CANNOT BE USED FOR COOKING OR FOOD PREPARATION. PIC WILL SWTICH TO FOOD SAFE UTENSILS BY THE TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Garbage and refuse properly disposed, facilities maintained

violations.title: Refuse Areas & Enclosures Maintained Clean
violations.observation: Trash and litter were observed adjacent to the refuse container outside the facility.
violations.corrective_action: A storage area and enclosure for refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall be maintained free of unnecessary items and kept clean. PIC UNDERSTANDS THAT THE AREA AROUND THR OUTSIDE DUMPSTERS NEED TO BE CLEANED BY THE TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair

violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities.
